item.title: Data Fabric: From Data to AI Apps
item.text: Connect authorized data sources to AI applications through a self-hosted gateway.

say.title: Data Fabric
say.text: [Data Fabric](#intro) connects authorized enterprise data to applications through one gateway.

item.title: Connect scattered data
item.prompt: A precise conceptual enterprise data network seen at a low isometric angle. On the left are three distinct database cylinders and a file archive; in the center a transparent luminous gateway cube; on the right two application panels and a compact AI node. Thin cyan paths connect the systems through the gateway while the source systems remain in place. Premium futuristic technical illustration, midnight navy background, luminous cyan and electric blue accents, restrained violet highlights, precision glass and metal forms, crisp studio lighting, clean widescreen composition. No text, no words, no labels.

say.title: From data to applications
say.text: [Enterprise data](#connected) often lives in business databases, analytics systems and object storage. Each application needs connections, authentication, query handling and result formats. The gateway centralizes those shared steps while data stays in the original systems.

say.title: An order-data scenario
say.text: [Order analysis](#business) connects the examples in this overview. [Orders](#orders) record transactions, [analytics](#analytics) supplies business summaries, and [files](#files) contain structured records. Authorized [applications and assistants](#assistants) find data, inspect its structure and retrieve results within their permissions.

say.title: A shared access path
say.text: [A request](#architecture) travels from an application through the gateway, where configured identity, permissions and routing are applied, to the target source. Results return through the same gateway. Teams can maintain one connection while authorized applications use separate identities.

say.title: Self-hosted deployment
say.text: [Self-hosted deployment](#deployment) runs the gateway in your own environment. A published image avoids local compilation. Prepare the required configuration, metadata storage and authentication, then start the services and use the health checks. Follow the guide for the exact release and profile.

say.title: Cross-source access
say.text: [Cross-source access](#federation) is optional. [Register a federation engine](#fed-register), let that engine [plan the cross-catalog query](#fed-plan), and [return results](#fed-result) through the gateway. Direct single-source requests use the corresponding driver.

say.title: Controlled sharing
say.text: [Controlled sharing](#security-hero) begins with the caller identity. The gateway applies configured owner, tenant and source permissions; a restricted database account adds a source-side boundary. Remote MCP requires the authentication and transport described in the release guide.

say.title: Table and column policies
say.text: [Access policies](#policy) can use [table rules](#pol-table) and [column rules](#pol-col) where supported. [Read-only validation](#pol-read) works alongside restricted source accounts, and [redacted audit events](#pol-audit) record access and query activity. Verify both allowed and denied paths in your environment.

say.title: Reuse across applications
say.text: [A shared source](#reuse) can serve a developer assistant, a desktop assistant and a business service. Each application uses its own configured identity, while the team maintains the connection in one place. Access remains subject to the grants that were actually configured and tested.

say.title: Application scenarios
say.text: [Applications](#apps) use the gateway in different workflows. [AI agents](#app-agent) obtain business context, [retrieval pipelines](#app-rag) read records for downstream processing, [text-to-SQL](#app-t2s) submits supported queries, and [business services](#app-api) use the API. Model inference and orchestration stay in the application stack.

Teams can distinguish a partially fetched result from a completed retrieval and review requests using the supported instrumentation.

say.title: Resource choices
say.text: [Resource use](#footprint) depends on the actual workload. [Connections](#foot-conn) are opened for configured sources, [routing](#foot-path) is selected for the task, and [batch and execution budgets](#foot-budget) can be tuned. The standard build includes registered drivers; measure startup time and memory on your own deployment.
